insights.concise_text: The proposed model addresses the less well-understood usefulness of Flickr for characterizing the natural environment by learning location vectors from Flickr tags and structured scientific information.

triple.subject: the proposed model
triple.object: the usefulness of Flickr for characterizing the natural environment

insights.concise_text: The paper replaces bag-of-words representations derived from Flickr tags with vector space embeddings to utilize ecological information more effectively.

triple.subject: vector space embeddings
triple.object: bag-of-words representations derived from Flickr tags

insights.concise_text: Because off-the-shelf GloVe performed surprisingly poorly, the model uses spatially smoothed PPMI scores and term selection to obtain better location vector spaces.

triple.subject: off-the-shelf GloVe model
triple.object: spatially smoothed PPMI scores and term selection

insights.concise_text: Vector space embeddings learned from Flickr tags alone are sometimes outperformed by bag-of-words representations, but structured scientific information makes vector space embeddings substantially better for predictions.

triple.subject: structured scientific information
triple.object: vector space embeddings learned from Flickr tags alone

insights.concise_text: Unlike POI embedding methods that often ignore textual information, the proposed work represents locations from Flickr tags plus numerical and categorical features from scientific datasets.

triple.subject: the proposed work
triple.object: POI embedding methods

insights.concise_text: The paper targets the far-from-optimal concatenation of Flickr tag bag-of-words features and structured scientific data with an embedding model whose components constrain textual, numerical, and categorical information.

triple.subject: the embedding model
triple.object: concatenation of Flickr tag bag-of-words features and structured scientific data

insights.concise_text: The 70 million Flickr photos with coordinates in Europe provide the Flickr tags whose PPMI scores replace co-occurrence statistics in the location embedding objective.

triple.subject: 70 million Flickr photos with coordinates in Europe
triple.object: PPMI scores in the location embedding objective

insights.concise_text: Because evaluating the full objective is not computationally feasible with millions of locations and millions of tags, the model samples negative examples rather than considering all tags.

triple.subject: computational infeasibility
triple.object: sampling negative examples rather than considering all tags

insights.concise_text: EGEL-All, the full method using Flickr tags and structured information, outperforms the baselines for all considered tasks, including binary classification tasks evaluated by macro average F1 score.

triple.subject: EGEL-All
triple.object: the baselines for all the considered tasks

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that the model integrates Flickr tags with structured information more effectively than existing methods is supported by EGEL-All outperforming the baselines for all considered tasks.

triple.subject: EGEL-All outperforming the baselines for all the considered tasks
triple.object: the conclusion that the model integrates Flickr tags with structured information more effectively than existing methods

insights.concise_text: Because EGEL-Tags only uses Flickr tags while EGEL-All additionally uses structured information, the consistent usefulness of embeddings for variants using both tags and structured datasets explains EGEL-All's advantage.

triple.subject: using both the tags and the structured datasets
triple.object: consistent usefulness of embeddings for predicting environmental features

insights.concise_text: The binary classification tasks of predicting the distribution of 100 species across Europe, soil type, and CORINE land cover classes at levels 1, 2 and level 3 are evaluated using Support Vector Machines (SVMs).

triple.subject: the binary classification tasks
triple.object: Support Vector Machines (SVMs)

insights.concise_text: The 26,425 distinct sites occurring in the Natura 2000 dataset define the shared location set INLINEFORM0 used for species distribution, soil type, CORINE land cover, and 5 climate related features experiments.

triple.subject: the 26,425 distinct sites occurring in the dataset
triple.object: the shared location set INLINEFORM0

insights.concise_text: The soil type, CORINE land cover, and 5 climate related features experiments exclude their target features from generating or constructing the embeddings, preventing direct use of those features as inputs.

triple.subject: the soil type, CORINE land cover, and 5 climate related features experiments
triple.object: excluding their target features from generating or constructing the embeddings

insights.concise_text: EGEL-Tags+NS adds negative examples to EGEL-Tags, and the addition of negative examples alleviates GloVe's worse performance than the bag-of-words model for smaller corpora.

triple.subject: the addition of negative examples
triple.object: GloVe's worse performance than the bag-of-words model for smaller corpora

insights.concise_text: The regression task predicting people's subjective opinions of landscape beauty in Britain uses the ScenicOrNot website ground truth and Support Vector Regression (SVR) predictions from geographic location representations.

triple.subject: predicting people's subjective opinions of landscape beauty in Britain
triple.object: Support Vector Regression (SVR)

insights.concise_text: The scenicness experiments use scores 3 and 7 as cut-off points to define three classes for KL divergence, while all experiments tune parameters with respect to Spearman INLINEFORM9 for regression tasks.

triple.subject: the scenicness experiments
triple.object: scores 3 and 7 as cut-off points, leading to three classes

insights.concise_text: EGEL-KL(Tags+NS) adds term selection to EGEL-Tags+NS, and term selection leads to particularly substantial improvements for the regression problems.

triple.subject: term selection
triple.object: the regression problems

item.text: The model builds on GloVe by treating tag occurrences as context words of geographic locations and learning location vectors instead of target word vectors.
The model integrates nine numerical features and 180 categorical features by predicting numerical values from location vectors and keeping same-category locations close together.
